label: early original-phase 0/x/n/o-type token (positions 2-3) after an i/v/u/a/b/p-initial sequence
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99% of mass), confined to steps t=1-3 (t=2 alone holds 63% of mass; never t=0, almost never t>=4, the delimiter, or the copy phase). It fires when the input is one of a small token set (0 strongest, then x, n, o, then e, c, 1, z), usually the first occurrence of that token. Magnitude is graded by context: much larger when the earlier tokens (especially the first token) are from {i, v, u, a, b, p} (top examples like "i i d [0]", "i v q [n]"). Restricting to that context gives precision about 0.5. Activation looks like an additive mix of input-token identity, position and prefix identity, not a sharp rule: the same token in a weaker context (e.g. after h, 1, n, q) fires weakly or not at all, and the right token after a favoured prefix sometimes does not fire. The predicate covers t=2-3 only, so it misses the weaker t=1 activations (about 15% of mass).
